children: Apple Inc.
dominated the week’s technology headlines, with developments spanning artificial intelligence, iPhones, wearable computing and internal operations.
The company’s strategy came under scrutiny from several directions, even as strong demand for premium iPhones offered investors a potentially brighter signal.
Here are five Apple stories that shaped the week, from AI privacy protections to a planned organizational overhaul.
Apple Takes Aim at AI Agents, Wants Mac Users to Know When Their Data Is Accessed as Meta Tackles Muse Privacy Claims

Apple wants Mac users to see when AI agents access data. The company plans to update macOS so users receive notifications whenever AI agents try to access system data, following criticism surrounding tools such as
Meta Platforms Inc.
Muse

Meta’s Muse has been accused of accessing private messages while completing complex tasks. Apple said its developer APIs support advanced app capabilities while preserving strict privacy controls, though the "Full Disk Access" permission can bypass many protections to support backup applications.
Read the full article
Jim Cramer Says ‘Buy’ Apple Stock Because of iPhone Duo, Not On Smart Home Device Buzz: Calls the $1,999 Foldable ‘Amazing’
On Wednesday,
Jim Cramer
urged investors to buy Apple stock because of what he called its "AMAZING" iPhone Duo, rather than excitement surrounding smart-home devices.

Apple shares rose 1.1% during regular trading before reaching $334.25 in after-hours trading, a 0.37% increase, according to Benzinga Pro. Cramer wrote on X, "Buy the stock of Apple because of the DUO, not smart home… Duo is AMAZING."
Read the full article
Is Apple’s Strategy Paying Off? Strong iPhone 18 Pro China Demand Sparks Revenue Upside

China demand is giving Apple’s premium strategy a boost. Early sales data for the iPhone 18 Pro series showed signs that Apple’s focus on higher-end models may be producing results, with delivery times extending across several major markets.
Counterpoint Research

reported 12% year-over-year growth for the iPhone 18 Pro lineup during its first three sales days. Apple also held the No. 1 position in China during Week 38, recording a 33% share of the smartphone market.
Read the full article
Apple Had the Blueprint for a Lighter Vision Pro But Scrapped It—Now Meta’s $1,299 VR Glasses Could Succeed Where AAPL Struggled

Apple’s abandoned lighter Vision Pro idea could get another chance. Years ago, the company reportedly explored a cheaper and lighter headset known internally as N107. The concept would have relied more heavily on an iPhone or Mac to reduce standalone processing and component demands.
Mark Gurman

wrote in his Power On newsletter that Apple ultimately abandoned the approach. Meanwhile, Meta has developed a similar concept into a mass-market product, with its $1,299 VR glasses potentially addressing limitations associated with Apple’s Vision Pro.
Read the full article
‘Beyond Spring and Fall’: Apple Prepares Organization Restructure for Accelerating Product Launches
Apple is preparing an organizational overhaul aimed at speeding product launches. Shares fell about 2% Tuesday as investors considered the restructuring under CEO
John Ternus
, while the broader market also weakened.
The Nasdaq was nearly unchanged and the S&P 500 declined 0.37%. Technology gained 0.09%, leaving Apple behind the sector despite strength among some mega-cap technology stocks.
